source_locators.locator: Main p. 2 (printed p. 388), Results paragraph: no obvious differences as Cu:Te decreases from 2:1 to 1.5:1 at otherwise unchanged conditions
Main p. 2 (printed p. 388), Results discussion of reduction to elemental metal and proposed nonuniform reactant dispersion

source_notes.note: The authors report no obvious differences for Cu:Te 2:1 to 1.5:1 at otherwise unchanged 160 °C/8 h conditions; 1.5:1 is prose context, not a separate Table 1 row. At 1.25:1 they report orthorhombic Cu2.86Te2 with Cu2-xTe; at 1:1 the product is predominantly Cu2.86Te2 with smaller amounts of CuTe, Cu7Te5 and Te. They propose that hydrazine hydrate reduction of metal ions to elemental metal at room temperature may leave reactants unevenly dispersed, contributing to different nonstoichiometric phases. This is the authors' proposed explanation, not an established mechanism.

claims.statement: Table 1 row at Cu:Te 1:1, 200 °C, 12 h lists Cu2.86Te2 with minor Te; CuTe is not listed.
Adjacent prose says higher reaction time and/or temperature increases CuTe while decreasing Te and Cu7Te5.

evidence_conflicts.resolution: Preserve both source statements; do not add CuTe to the exact table row.
